title: processkit-cli JSONL lifecycle-event stream (v1)
description: One line of processkit-cli's `--jsonl` lifecycle-event stream. This is the machine-readable mirror of the normative prose in docs/schema.md; docs/schema.md is the source of truth on any discrepancy. Each event object shares a common envelope (`schema_version`, `time`, `event`) plus fields specific to its `event` type tag. Validated against `fixtures/schema/v1/events.jsonl` (the golden fixture) by `tests/events.rs`.

time.description: Emission time, RFC 3339 UTC, millisecond precision (`…Z`).

member.description: One entry of a members_snapshot. `ppid`/`name`/`start_time` are filled from ProcessKit's members_info() wherever the platform can report them; each stays independently null where it can't (docs/schema.md, 'Enriched member fields').

ppid.description: Parent pid; null where the platform can't report it.

name.description: Executable name; null where the platform can't report it.

start_time.description: Opaque, platform-specific start-time token as a decimal string (not a timestamp); null where the platform can't report it.

commandInfo.description: The command a run executed, in its redaction-aware v1 shape (docs/schema.md, 'Command redaction').

redacted.description: true by default; false only under --argv-raw.

argv.description: The raw argv, present only when redacted is false; null otherwise.

argv_sha256.description: Lowercase-hex SHA-256 fingerprint of argv; filled on every run regardless of redaction (docs/schema.md, 'Fingerprint').

hint.description: Worker-shape hint for a recognized argv (e.g. msbuild_node_reuse), else null (docs/schema.md, 'Hint classifier').

path.description: The file the stream was written to.

bytes.description: Full byte counter; exceeds the file size when truncated or a write failed.

sha256.description: Lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the bytes actually written to path.

truncated.description: true when the stream outran the per-stream capture ceiling.

write_error.description: true when a file write failed part-way through the stream.

runStarted.description: The run has begun: the child is spawned into the container.

run_id.description: The --run-id value, or a generated run-<pid>-<unix_nanos>.

labels.description: Operator-provided run labels, empty when none were supplied.

root_pid.description: The root child's PID; null if the backend exposed none.

cwd.description: The child's absolute working directory; null if it could not be resolved.

membersSnapshot.description: A point-in-time snapshot of the container's members. Emitted once right after run_started (reason 'spawn'); a run given --snapshot-interval additionally re-emits it on that cadence (reason 'interval') until the ending is decided (docs/schema.md, 'members_snapshot' and 'Ordering').

reason.description: What asked for this snapshot: 'spawn' (once, right after the child was spawned) or 'interval' (a --snapshot-interval re-sample).

read_error.description: true when the members_info() read itself failed; `members` is then an empty fallback, not a confirmed-empty tree. The sample is recorded rather than skipped so the failure is visible in the stream itself — the only channel a detached run has, its stderr being null (docs/schema.md, 'members_snapshot').

rootExited.description: The root child exited on its own.

code.description: The exit code for exited; null otherwise.

signal.description: The signal number for a Unix signalled death; null otherwise.

members_before.description: The tree size (member count) about to be reaped.

read_error.description: true when the pre-cleanup member read itself failed, in which case members_before is a 0 fallback, not a confirmed empty tree.

cleanupFinished.description: Container teardown finished (after the hard kill).

soft_terminate.description: The soft-stop tier for a runner-imposed ending; null on the natural-exit path.

shutdown.description: ProcessKit capability and ShutdownReport observations for a runner-imposed graceful teardown; null when no soft stop was attempted.

read_error.description: true when the post-kill member read itself failed, in which case remaining/remaining_pids fall back to an empty snapshot, not a confirmed-clean teardown.

limitHit.description: A requested ProcessKit resource limit (--max-memory/--max-processes/--cpu-quota) could not be applied. Emitted pre-spawn, only for the 'could not be applied' branch (Unsupported/Unenforceable), immediately before the container_failed(create) -> runner_exit(container_error) tail; nonsense values are rejected earlier as USAGE. docs/schema.md ('limit_hit') is the source of truth.

limit.description: Which limit could not be applied: memory, processes, or cpu.

limitEvidence.description: Post-run per-axis evidence for a run whose requested cap was successfully installed in a ProcessGroup. Each value is tripped, not_tripped, or unknown; the event is absent when no cap was requested or ProcessGroup creation failed before spawn.

resourceSummary.description: What the contained tree actually consumed, read once from the container's own kernel accounting (ProcessGroup::stats()) after the ending is decided and before teardown consumes the group. Emitted by every run that spawned the child - no flag, no cap required, every platform - exactly once. Every measurement is independently nullable and null always means 'this mechanism does not account for it', never zero and never a value improved by taking a maximum over the runner's own periodic reads; read_error true means the read itself failed, which is the only thing distinguishing that from a mechanism that legitimately accounts for nothing. docs/schema.md ('resource_summary') is the source of truth and docs/resource-limits.md ('What the tree consumed') carries the normative platform matrix.

read_error.description: true when the stats() read itself failed, in which case every measurement below is null as a gap rather than as a mechanism's confirmed 'not accounted'. The event is emitted either way.

peak_memory_bytes.description: Peak whole-tree memory in bytes; null where the mechanism keeps no accumulator (macOS/BSD, the POSIX fallback). Platform-specific in meaning and not comparable across platforms: a Windows Job Object reports peak committed memory (PeakJobMemoryUsed), a Linux cgroup v2 the sum of currently-live members' peak resident sets.

total_cpu_ms.description: Total CPU time (user + kernel) the tree accumulated, in milliseconds - the unit every other duration in this schema uses. Truncated toward zero, so a run that used under a millisecond of CPU reports a measured 0; null is the only value meaning unknown. Windows counts every process ever in the job, Linux cgroup v2 only currently-live members.

io_read_bytes.description: Bytes the tree read; null where the mechanism does not account for IO - always on macOS/BSD and the POSIX fallback, and on Linux unless the cgroup v2 'io' controller is enabled (this runner does not enable it). Not comparable across platforms: a Job Object counts all read traffic whatever the target, cgroup io.stat only what crossed the block layer.

io_write_bytes.description: Bytes the tree wrote, the write half of io_read_bytes with the same per-platform meaning and the same honest null. On Linux this is block-layer writeback, which can land after the member that dirtied the page exited - or not at all if the group is torn down first - so a short write-and-exit run may report fewer bytes than it handed to write(2).

peak_process_count.description: High-water mark of processes held at once; null where the mechanism keeps no such counter, which is ALWAYS the case on Windows (a Job Object tracks only 'now' and 'ever assigned', neither of which is a peak). On Linux it is the pids controller's pids.peak, which charges every task, so it equals a process count only while every member is single-threaded.

timeout.description: A runner deadline elapsed while the child was still running: the whole-run --timeout or the --idle-timeout (no child output for the idle window). Both share this event and the reserved TIMEOUT (106) code; `reason` tells them apart.

timeout_ms.description: The deadline that elapsed, milliseconds (the whole-run window for overall, the idle window for idle).

grace_ms.description: The --grace window, ms; null if unset.

reason.description: Which deadline fired: overall (--timeout) or idle (--idle-timeout).

outputOverflow.description: A capture stream exceeded its per-stream byte ceiling while --capture-overflow cancel was active. The run then enters the shared graceful teardown and exits with OUTPUT_OVERFLOW (113).

stream.description: The first stream to cross the ceiling.

grace_ms.description: The --grace window, ms; null if unset.

cancelled.description: The run was cancelled and torn down through the shared soft-stop -> grace -> hard-kill path.

source.description: ctrl_c for a local interactive Ctrl-C; sigterm/sighup (Unix) for the stop signals the runner catches - an external kill/systemctl stop/cancelled CI job, or a hung-up controlling terminal; ctrl_break/ctrl_close/ctrl_logoff/ctrl_shutdown (Windows) for the console-control events the runner catches; control_cancel for a control-plane cancel. The local signals/events share the CANCELLED (107) terminal code; control_cancel takes CONTROL_CANCELLED (108).

grace_ms.description: The effective --grace window, ms; null if unset. For a Windows ctrl_close this may be less than the requested --grace, capped to fit the OS's own termination window; every other trigger echoes the request unchanged.

killed.description: The run was killed by a control-plane kill command: an immediate hard kill of the whole tree, with no soft stop and no grace.

spawnFailed.description: The program could not be started (not found, not executable, bad --cwd): the child never ran.

containerFailed.description: Creating the container, joining the child to it, or handing the terminal to an interactive child failed.

phase.description: create (the container could not be created), attach (the launch into it failed), or foreground (handing the terminal to an interactive child failed after it had already spawned).

runnerExit.description: The terminal event of every run: the exact code the runner process returns.

code.description: The exit code the runner process returns (child's code, or a runner-band code).

child_code.description: The child's own exit code when it exited on its own; null for a runner-imposed ending or a child that never produced one.

outputCaptured.description: Bounded stdout/stderr capture finished. Emitted only when run was given --capture-dir.
